Machine Learning (ML): Learns patterns from data using algorithms like decision trees, SVMs, or regression.
Deep Learning (DL): Learns complex representations using multi-layered neural networks that mimic the human brain.

Machine Learning (ML): Requires manual feature selection — data scientists must choose and transform features.
Deep Learning (DL): Automatically extracts features from raw data with minimal human intervention.

Machine Learning (ML): Works well with small to medium datasets.
Deep Learning (DL): Needs large amounts of data to perform well and avoid overfitting.

Machine Learning (ML): Runs efficiently on CPUs; less hardware-intensive.
Deep Learning (DL): Requires high-performance GPUs/TPUs due to heavy matrix computations.

Machine Learning (ML): Easier to explain and visualize (e.g., decision trees, linear regression).
Deep Learning (DL): Often seen as a black box — harder to interpret how decisions are made.

Machine Learning (ML): Fast to train; suitable for quick experimentation.
Deep Learning (DL): Very time-intensive due to millions of parameters and iterative optimization.

Machine Learning (ML): Limited — struggles with unstructured data like images, audio, and natural language.
Deep Learning (DL): Excels at complex, high-dimensional data (vision, speech, NLP).

Machine Learning (ML): High — human intuition guides model design and feature creation.
Deep Learning (DL): Low — the model learns representations automatically from raw input.

Machine Learning (ML): Simpler architectures, fewer parameters.
Deep Learning (DL): Deep architectures with multiple hidden layers and millions of parameters.

Machine Learning (ML): Lightweight, easy to deploy and update.
Deep Learning (DL): Heavy and complex; needs specialized infrastructure for deployment.

Machine Learning (ML): Linear Regression, Random Forest, SVM, K-Means.
Deep Learning (DL): CNNs (image), RNNs/LSTMs (text), Transformers (language models).

Machine Learning (ML): Structured data, tabular datasets, small-scale business analytics.
Deep Learning (DL): Unstructured data, computer vision, NLP, speech recognition, autonomous systems.

Machine Learning (ML): Easier to detect and correct model errors; simpler debugging process.
Deep Learning (DL): Error detection is harder due to complex inter-layer dependencies.

Machine Learning (ML): Highly scalable for small and medium datasets but less efficient on very large-scale systems.
Deep Learning (DL): Highly scalable — performs better with distributed GPU/TPU clusters.

Machine Learning (ML): Consumes less energy due to lighter computations.
Deep Learning (DL): Energy-hungry; requires more power for training and inference.

Machine Learning (ML): Moderate — can be controlled with regularization and cross-validation.
Deep Learning (DL): High risk — can easily overfit without large data or dropout techniques.

Machine Learning (ML): Easier to retrain or update models incrementally without high costs.
Deep Learning (DL): Updating models requires retraining large networks — computationally expensive.

Machine Learning (ML): Requires significant domain and statistical expertise for best performance.
Deep Learning (DL): Less dependent on human expertise once designed — relies on data volume and architecture tuning.

Machine Learning (ML): Low latency — suitable for real-time and edge applications.
Deep Learning (DL): May have higher latency due to complex computations in deep layers.

Machine Learning (ML): Interpretability tools are mature (e.g., SHAP, LIME).
Deep Learning (DL): Explainability tools are emerging (e.g., Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradients).

Machine Learning (ML): Primarily suited for structured, numerical, and categorical data.
Deep Learning (DL): Handles structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data seamlessly.

Machine Learning (ML): Can be adapted easily to new problems by modifying features and algorithms.
Deep Learning (DL): Shows strong transfer learning capabilities — can adapt to new tasks with minimal retraining.
